title: The UN political-process mandate
summary: OSE-Syria's public mandate page describes support for a Syrian-led political process guided by Security Council resolution 2254. This identifies an institutional frame for research; it does not describe which political arrangements are currently implemented.

evidence.locator: Mandate text on the Syrian-led process and resolution 2254
UN resolution metadata and adoption date

scope.temporal: Institutional self-description checked 2 November 2026; resolution adopted in 2015.

questions: Which recent official statements explain how the office applies this mandate?
Which documented commitments, processes and contested questions should be distinguished?
limits: Do not infer current electoral dates, constitutional arrangements, representation or territorial control from the 2015 resolution.
Current_verified_fact refers only to the office's published institutional self-description.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: How can participation be examined?
summary: Research question: what published evidence shows who can participate in a political process, how proposals are considered and how excluded voices can be heard? Examine women, civil society, displaced people and diverse communities without treating any selected interview or consultation as nationally representative.

evidence.locator: Mandate discussion of Syrian ownership and meaningful participation of women

scope.temporal: Prospective research prompt, not a finding.

proposed_outputs: A dated participation matrix identifying the process, invitation criteria, participants, published outcomes and acknowledged gaps.
A short analytical note separating official consultation design from reported participant experience.
limits: This is a proposed analytical method; it makes no claim that a particular current process is inclusive or exclusionary.
Additional first-hand reporting and current primary documents would be needed to answer it.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: Community relations and protection needs
summary: UNHCR's Q2 protection report describes social-cohesion concerns and psychosocial distress in coastal consultations, and access and safety concerns in its southern regional findings. These dated observations can inform questions about pluralism and equal access to services.

evidence.locator: p.23 §9.3 Coastal Region; p.24 §9.5 Southern Region; p.4 methodology

questions: Which findings concern rights, which concern access to services and which are perceptions reported by respondents?
What more recent evidence supports, qualifies or contradicts these observations?
limits: Do not generalize a regional consultation into the view of an entire community.
Do not use Q2 findings as a present-day safety map or infer current collective intentions.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: Return movements and sustainable reintegration
summary: UNHCR's 29 October dashboard presents estimated refugee returns with a governorate breakdown and explains the triangulation of movement and border-monitoring data. Its Q2 protection monitoring provides separate evidence about reintegration constraints.

evidence.locator: Dashboard title, key-figure estimation note and governorate overview

scope.temporal: Returns dashboard as of 29 October 2026; reintegration monitoring from Q2 2026.

questions: How do return estimates differ from evidence about housing, documentation, services and livelihoods?
Which definitions and reporting dates permit a valid comparison between agencies or rounds?
limits: A return estimate does not establish that an individual return was voluntary, safe or sustainable.
Do not mix refugee returns, IDP returns and border crossings or sum overlapping datasets.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: Investigation, attribution and accountability
summary: The Commission of Inquiry's A/HRC/55/64 explains its investigative approach, evidentiary standard and distinction from a judicial body. Use it as a methodology reference when separating documented findings, attribution, allegations and judicial decisions.

evidence.locator: Section I, Mandate and methodology, paragraphs 1–2

scope.temporal: Historical report dated 9 February 2024, covering July–December 2023.

questions: What does a source establish under its own mandate and standard of proof?
Is a claim a witness account, an investigative finding, a general attribution or a court decision?
limits: No incident findings from this historical report are presented as current facts.
Do not infer present criminal liability, current legal status or a current court ruling from a commission report.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: Services as part of reintegration
summary: UNHCR's September update reports work on community protection, legal support, housing repairs and livelihoods. It also describes a new community centre in Al-Shaddadi. These are dated programme accounts, not a comprehensive assessment of public-service performance.

evidence.locator: pp.2–4: protection, shelter, livelihoods and return support

scope.geography: Syria; activities in named towns and governorates

questions: Which service constraints affect returnees and host communities?
What distinguishes a planned project, an activity delivered and evidence of an outcome?
limits: Do not infer current opening hours, availability, coverage or completed outcomes from a monthly activity report.
Whole-programme totals must not be assigned to an individual town or governorate.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: What makes recovery durable?
summary: Proposed research: examine how income opportunities, housing costs, civil documentation and essential services interact in household recovery. Compare primary monitoring with economic research, identify what can actually be measured and test rival explanations before proposing an intervention.

evidence.locator: Executive summary and regional findings, pp.3 and 23–24

scope.temporal: Prospective research agenda anchored to dated monitoring.

proposed_outputs: A source-linked constraint map for one defined locality and reporting period.
An 800–1,200-word research brief with observable indicators, competing explanations and explicit evidence gaps.
limits: This is a project proposal, not a forecast or causal finding.
No current sanctions rule, macroeconomic figure, legal banking status or investment recommendation is asserted.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.

title: Humanitarian coordination has a distinct mandate
summary: The UN Geneva organizational profile describes OCHA's mission as coordinating principled humanitarian action with national and international partners, advocating for people in need and supporting preparedness. This helps distinguish humanitarian coordination from political mediation or judicial investigation.

scope.geography: Global institutional role, relevant to Syria research

questions: Which institution is responsible for the activity being analysed?
Does a cited document describe coordination, service delivery, political facilitation or investigation?
limits: This is an institutional mission statement, not evidence that a particular response or access arrangement is operating now.
Do not infer command authority over other agencies, political parties or judicial bodies.
review_note: Typed research context; institutional pages establish a published remit, not implementation or present conditions.
